content: The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
author: Carl Sagan
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Carl Sagan saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
